data.name: Inshaf
data.gender_notes: Inshaf is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Inshaf is a name derived from the Arabic root 'Sh-F-F', which means 'to heal, to cure, or to provide a remedy'. In Islamic tradition, it is believed that Allah (God) grants Inshaf (healing) to those who seek His help and guidance. In the Quran, Surah Ar-Ra'd (verses 81-82) mentions, 'And indeed, there came to them a Messenger from Allah confirming that which was with them. And a wounded party from among them were doubtful about (their) religion. So he (Muhammad SAW) said: 'Verily, with Allah is the criterion (of right and wrong). He is Allah, the All-Knower.' This event signifies the importance of faith and trust in Allah for healing and guidance.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing Allah's healing power and guidance.
data.etymology: Inshaf belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Healing, Cure, Remedy.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Inshaf total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: نشانف

historical_references.context: Inshaf is a title given to a book authored by the third son of the Twelfth Imam, Al-Qa'im bi-Amrillah. The book was written in response to the doubts and questions of a group of scholars regarding the Imam's absence and the signs of his return. The title Inshaf means 'revelation' or 'manifestation', reflecting the idea that the book would bring clarification and guidance to the matter of the Imam's absence.
